objective: Typeless-style push-to-talk hotkeys for the Windows desktop app. (1) New engine-agnostic module voice2txt/hotkeys.py: VK code <-> display-name table (at least RightAlt 0xA5, LeftAlt 0xA4, RightShift 0xA1, LeftShift 0xA0, RightCtrl 0xA3, LeftCtrl 0xA2, Space 0x20, CapsLock 0x14, F1-F12 0x70-0x7B, and generic Alt/Shift/Ctrl that match either side); combo parse/format ('RightAlt+RightShift' <-> 'Right Alt + Right Shift'); a pure-Python PushToTalk state machine with an injectable clock: configured actions 'dictate' and 'translate', each with up to 2 combos; input is (vk, is_down, now); output events ('start', action) / ('stop', None); semantics: all keys of a combo held -> start; releasing any key after holding >= 0.35 s -> stop (hold-to-talk); releasing within 0.35 s -> tap: recording stays on until the same combo is tapped again (tap-to-toggle); when a pressed key set is a strict prefix of a longer configured combo, defer start by a 0.15 s grace (resolved by tick(now)) so RightAlt+RightShift wins over RightAlt; auto-repeat key-down events are ignored; unrelated keys are ignored; the machine also reports whether an event was consumed as a hotkey. (2) Win32 LowLevelKeyboardHook class in the same module (ctypes, WH_KEYBOARD_LL = 13, HOOKPROC with KBDLLHOOKSTRUCT, own thread with a GetMessageW loop, clean uninstall via PostThreadMessageW WM_QUIT); it never swallows keys (return CallNextHookEx) so AltGr layouts keep working; to stop a bare Alt tap from activating the focused app's menu bar, when the state machine consumed a bare Alt press it injects a no-op key (SendInput/keybd_event with VK 0xFF) right before the Alt key-up passes through. Events go to a callback (the app puts them on its events queue). (3) desktop.py: replace the RegisterHotKey thread with the hook; add a '口述語言' setting (繁體中文 / English) used by the 'dictate' action; 'translate' action records in translate mode; the mode combobox keeps controlling the manual button; hotkey start/stop reuse toggle()/stop() with the session mode set from the action; keep the target-window capture and paste-back behaviour; new settings section '快捷鍵' with, per action, the current combo label(s), a '設定' button that captures the next pressed key combination from the hook (shows it live, confirms on full release), a '清除' button, and '再加一個' for a second combo; defaults dictate = RightAlt (plus the legacy Alt+Shift+Space as second combo), translate = RightAlt+RightShift; persist as settings['hotkeys'] = {'dictate': ['RightAlt', 'Alt+Shift+Space'], 'translate': ['RightAlt+RightShift']}; update the help label under the editor. (4) tests/test_hotkeys.py covering parse/format round-trip, hold-release, tap-toggle, prefix grace and longer-combo precedence, auto-repeat and unrelated keys, generic Alt matching both sides, max two combos. (5) scripts/check_hotkey_hook.py: real Win32 check that installs the hook, injects Right Alt down/up with SendInput (hold 0.5 s), then a tap, then RightAlt+RightShift, and asserts the emitted start/stop/action sequence; also asserts GetForegroundWindow is unchanged; writes verification/hotkey-hook-2026-11-13.json with ok=true.
acceptance: `.\.build-venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest discover -s tests -v` passes; tests/test_hotkeys.py has at least 8 tests and none of them touch Win32 (they must pass with the hook class never instantiated).

`.\.build-venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts\check_hotkey_hook.py` writes verification/hotkey-hook-2026-11-13.json with ok=true and the observed event sequence [('start','dictate'),('stop',None),('start','dictate'),('stop',None),('start','translate'),('stop',None)] (hold, tap-tap, combo hold) and foreground_unchanged=true.
`$env:PYTHONPATH='.'; .\.build-venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts\smoke_desktop.py` passes and `run_desktop.py --self-test` still reports ok=true, desktop_ui=true.

grep: desktop.py no longer calls RegisterHotKey; settings.json written by the app contains a 'hotkeys' object with the defaults above; the capture UI exists ('設定' and '再加一個' buttons present in the 快捷鍵 section).
No key is swallowed: the hook procedure always returns CallNextHookEx (grep shows no early `return 1` path).
notes: Python 3.9, stdlib + ctypes only (no pynput/keyboard packages). All UI strings Traditional Chinese. Keep the Tk thread rule: the hook thread only puts events on the queue; UI changes happen in _poll. Do not touch translation.py, tests/test_translation.py or the iOS files. Do not run git.
